rules.intent: Nontrivial code implementation, debugging, code correctness review, or difficult technical problem solving. The deliverable is reliable working code, rather than documentation or a plan.
Read and analyze many files, trace architecture or dependencies, compare evidence, or answer fact-sensitive technical questions. Primarily analysis, rather than implementing code.
Design a solution, plan a multi-step project, organize an agent workflow, or weigh architecture tradeoffs before coding. The requested deliverable is a design or plan.
Write or translate documentation, draft prose, summarize supplied material, or general non-coding synthesis. The deliverable is text, rather than code, an engineering plan, or a short factual answer.
A greeting, a short straightforward factual or syntax question, a small mechanical edit or rename in one location, or another simple routine task needing little analysis.
Nontrivial multi-file or stateful implementation, or difficult debugging. The deliverable is reliable working code.
Complex logic, algorithms, data flow, or long-context edits spanning many files.
Well-specified feature implementation with clear requirements, where speed matters.
Standard features or test suites: routine implementation needing reliability.
Standard Codex-native patch workflows: apply_patch edits and patch-and-test loops.
Config files, scripts, or other straightforward small edits.
Native patch-and-test implementation: apply_patch edits and multi-step test workflows.
Logic-heavy implementation: complex algorithms or intricate code paths with tests.
Bounded feature or test implementation with clear scope, where speed matters.
Standard TDD steps and test suites: routine red-green implementation.
Straightforward tasks, scripts, or config changes.
Hard implementation: architecture, auth, migrations, or concurrency.
Algorithm-heavy or long-context implementation.
Multi-file feature implementation with clear scope, where speed matters.
Multi-step patch and test workflows, native implementation.
Lighter integration or infrastructure tasks.
Complex or high-risk code review: security, concurrency, or large multi-file diffs.
Thorough code quality, architecture, or bug review.
Review of complex logic or long-context diffs spanning many files.
Review of bounded feature diffs with clear scope, where speed matters.
High-precision review where low false-positive rate matters.
Routine review of standard task diffs.
Small diffs or scoped fix re-reviews.
Root-cause debugging: clear failures through subtle multi-module bugs.
Elusive root-cause analysis requiring high factual precision.
Multi-file call-chain or state-bug analysis.
Algorithmic, data-flow, or long-trace debugging.
Runtime, config, or environment failures.
Localized unit test failures.
Standard repository exploration: symbol search, file lookup, or tracing references.
Broad multi-file architecture discovery, cross-module tracing, or understanding a large unfamiliar codebase.
High-accuracy search or dependency lookup where precision matters and false leads are costly.
Standard spec or plan review, through complex architecture.
Broad multi-file interface and requirement consistency checks.
Architectural and requirement review.
Simple, well-bounded plan review.
Hardest, highest-risk audits only: system-wide architecture, security, or concurrency specs.
Standard repository exploration: symbol search, file lookup, or tracing references.
Broad multi-file architecture discovery, cross-module tracing, or understanding a large unfamiliar codebase.
High-accuracy search or dependency lookup where precision matters and false leads are costly.
Complex engineering, difficult technical reasoning, or nontrivial implementation. The deliverable is reliable working code or a hard technical answer.
Complex multi-file analysis or fact-critical reasoning, where factual precision matters more than code output.
General reasoning, synthesis, or multi-step planning before acting.
Documentation, prose, summaries, or medium-complexity synthesis. The deliverable is text rather than code.
A straightforward routine task, simple question, or small mechanical edit needing little analysis.
